questions.q: In 'The Spendthrift and the Swallow', why did the young man sell his clothes?
choices: He saw a Swallow and thought summer had come
His clothes were too old and full of holes
He wanted the money to buy a pet Swallow
His friends told him to sell them for a feast

questions.q: What is the lesson of 'The Spendthrift and the Swallow'?
choices: One swallow does not make a summer
Always save your money for the cold days
Birds can always tell the weather
Warm clothes are best in winter
questions.evidence: One swallow does not make a summer.

questions.q: In 'The Cat and the Birds', what did the Cat pretend to be?
choices: A doctor
A teacher
A mail carrier
A farmer
questions.evidence: Dr. Cat, with much solicitude, asked how they were

questions.q: The moral of 'The Cat and the Birds' says to 'shun the quack.' Here, a 'quack' is:
choices: A fake doctor who tricks people
The loud sound a duck makes
A sick bird that cannot fly
A real doctor who heals
questions.evidence: Be wise and shun the quack.

questions.q: In 'The Dog and the Oyster', why did the Dog swallow the Oyster?
choices: He thought it was an egg
He was told oysters taste good
He wanted to find a pearl
Another dog dared him to
questions.evidence: I've learned that all round things are not eggs

questions.q: In 'The Astrologer', what happened while the man was staring at the stars?
choices: He fell into a hole full of mud and water
He saw a sign in the stars of the end of the world
He found a lost gold coin in the road
He walked straight into a big tree
questions.evidence: down he went into a hole full of mud and water

questions.q: What is the lesson of 'The Astrologer'?
choices: Take care of little things and big things take care of themselves
Always look up at the stars at night to learn about the future
Never walk alone on a dark road outside of the village
The future is written in the stars for anyone who can read it
questions.evidence: Take care of the little things and the big things will take care of themselves.

questions.q: In 'Three Bullocks and a Lion', why was the Lion finally able to eat the Bullocks?
choices: They quarreled and stayed apart from each other
They grew old and weak and could not fight any longer
The Lion brought other lions to help him
They fell asleep together in the field
questions.evidence: he found them in separate corners of the field

questions.q: What is the lesson of 'Three Bullocks and a Lion'?
choices: In unity is strength
Lions are the strongest
Never eat in an open field
Sharp horns keep you safe
